hook: The Prophet of Islam, who united Arabia under the faith in one God.

pages.x: Muhammad was born in Mecca around 570. His father died before he was born and his mother when he was six; he was raised by his grandfather, then by his uncle Abu Talib, a merchant. As a young man he led trading caravans to Syria and was known as al-Amin, "the trustworthy".

At 25 he married Khadija, a widow and successful merchant about 15 years older than him, who had hired him to lead her caravans. They were married for 25 years, and she was the first person to believe in his message.

He often went to pray alone in a cave on a mountain outside Mecca. Muslims believe that one night in 610 the angel Gabriel appeared to him there and commanded "Recite!", giving him the first words of the Quran. He came home trembling, and Khadija comforted him.

He began to preach that there is only one God, and that people must care for the poor and for orphans. The leaders of Mecca, who grew rich from pilgrims to the idols around the Kaaba, mocked and persecuted his followers. Some fled to Christian Ethiopia for safety.

In 622, warned of a plot to kill him, he escaped to the town of Yathrib, later called Medina, "the city". Tradition says he hid in a cave on the way, while a spider spun its web across the entrance and fooled his pursuers. The Islamic calendar counts its years from this journey.
pages.cap: Mount Thawr, where he hid in a cave

pages.x: In Medina he led a growing community and fought several battles with Mecca. In 630 he returned at the head of 10,000 followers, and Mecca surrendered almost without bloodshed. He forgave most of his old enemies and cleared the idols from the Kaaba.

In 632 he made a last pilgrimage to Mecca and told a vast crowd that all believers are equal: "An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab." He died in Medina a few months later and was buried in his mosque there.

Muhammad founded Islam, today the faith of nearly two billion people. Within a century of his death it reached from Spain to India, and the Quran made Arabic a language of prayer and learning across the world.
pts: The Prophet of Islam, followed by nearly two billion people
Brought the Quran, as Muslims believe, revealed by God
